source_text: dixerimus, ita colligis, "minus peccare adulteros quam maritos; quia maritis libido servit ut peccent, adulteris imperat Libidinem, si mala est, maiori reatu obstringere quibus obsequitur coniuges, quam quibus dominatur adulteros
pass_a_gloss: Dixerimus, so colligis, " less peccare adulteros than/which maritos; because maritis lust servit so-that/as peccent, adulteris imperat lust, if evils is, greater in-guilt obstringere to-whom obsequitur coniuges, than/which to-whom dominatur adulteros.

lemmas.lexica: LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis

pass_b_english: When it serves married people for producing offspring, lust is then honored.
Adulterers sin less than married people, because lust serves married people so that they sin, while it commands adulterers.
If lust is evil, it binds married people whom it serves with greater guilt than adulterers whom it rules.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
